calls.call_name: Ramsay Scholars Research Grant Program 2026

eligibility.career_stage: PhD students; postdocs; early-stage investigators (first 5 years of independent programme); established investigators new to ME/CFS, Long COVID or related conditions; faculty returning after career breaks; collaborative teams of 2+ institutions or groups
eligibility.country: No country restriction stated in the RFP; past awardees include European groups
eligibility.institution_must_be_nonprofit: Not stated; indirect costs capped at 10%
eligibility.non_academics_can_apply: Not stated; the RFP is written for academic investigators
eligibility.notes: Two stages: ~800-word initial research plan plus CV; invited full proposals get double-blind review. Must focus on ME/CFS, Long COVID or another infection-associated chronic condition (IACC) with a clear ME/CFS or Long COVID link. Pre-pandemic cohorts, biobanks and registry data are encouraged.

amount.text: PhD award $50k for 1 year; postdoc/new/returning faculty up to $100k over 2 years; collaborative up to $150k over 2 years

deadline.text: Initial research plan due 13 Nov 2026; full-proposal invitations 4 Dec 2026; full proposals due 8 Jan 2027; decisions 8 Feb 2027

calls.fit_notes: Best near-term fit for any pilot: covers multi-omics, vascular biology, neuroimmune work, and use of biobank or registry data. A crash-window (PEM) sampling pilot or a pituitary/serum-factor pilot fits the $100k-150k tiers.

eligibility.notes: No public application call. Awards go to selected projects; enquiries to Research@SolveCFS.org.

deadline.text: No open call; awards announced several times a year (Feb, May, Jul 2026)

calls.fit_notes: Suits projects that already have data and need completion funding. The SIGNAL device-lending award shows that decentralised tracking platforms qualify.

calls.call_name: Researching ME/CFS: priority area (highlight notice across all MRC schemes)

eligibility.career_stage: Per scheme: new investigators, established PIs, fellows. International co-leads allowed if they bring unique expertise.
eligibility.country: UK research organisations eligible for UKRI funding
eligibility.institution_must_be_nonprofit: UKRI-eligible research organisations (universities, institutes, some NHS/IROs)
eligibility.notes: Priorities from the JLA Priority Setting Partnership: PEM mechanism, repurposed drugs, diagnostic test, immune/autoimmune, stratification, post-infection onset, neurological, genetics, severity, mitochondria, oxygen delivery. Contact mecfs@mrc.ukri.org.

amount.text: No cap; MRC usually pays 80% of full economic cost (FEC)

deadline.text: Open, no closing date (in place since 2003; updated 18 May 2026). Applicant-led schemes are open all year, with funding decisions in June and December.

calls.fit_notes: The main UK route. A PEM-mechanism study combining crash-window sampling and circulatory phenotyping maps directly to PSP priority #1 and 'oxygen delivery'.

calls.call_name: Wellcome Discovery Awards

eligibility.career_stage: Established researchers with international standing; teams of 2-8 led by an established researcher. Co-applicants can be at any career stage, anywhere except mainland China.
eligibility.country: From 29 Oct 2026 the lead applicant must be based in the UK or an eligible low/middle-income country (Africa, South and South-East Asia)
eligibility.institution_must_be_nonprofit: No: co-applicants can be at HEIs, research institutes, healthcare organisations, charities, social enterprises or commercial organisations
eligibility.non_academics_can_apply: Co-applicants yes; the lead must hold a long-term contract at an eligible organisation
eligibility.notes: Discovery research: bold ideas, new tools and methods

amount.text: Ask for what you need; average £3.5M; >£5M gets extra scrutiny

deadline.text: No deadlines; apply any time

calls.fit_notes: For an established London PI building a multi-year ME/CFS mechanism programme. The new UK-only rule favours London leads.
